canonical.head: c28bd8e83d0b88a9dba0c0a9fdbd35a25e6ecd07
canonical.body:
## Runtime owner and non-negotiable architecture
The product is **M3JDK21 itself**, not M3 layered onto JDK. This PR publishes the canonical Synexia **recipe and algorithm catalogue before product mutation**. It reuses the existing `M3HashPinnedJavaSnapshotRecipe` OpenRewrite source-LST host, and has no Synexia runtime dependency.

## Exact candidate
- Target existing product owner: `m3/core/src/com/m3/text/M3GvasLiteralImage.java`; original Git blob `32f506b95688b6cdc11fdf6573a6baaa9ee608c8`.
- Source SHA-256: `f3ed3fd91d7e60220ba22e717f6fec41dc7759e5a221ef1dba65251d0028f8d7` -> `2c1a8b9cc9870fc5fdf8e6f8ca46af907c503346aaf6d783b74a6498fd3601cd`.
- JNI contract test source SHA-256: `b81541431b6eb57e0d8d200d0a65a1a67cc5e9a3022ac8363d401ea4bdd44a3e` -> `9bb67410bda500c43eb58f65c648351fc1ac477328abe84da2537bab823f114d`.
- Named OpenRewrite recipe `com.synexia.m3.GvasPrimitiveHash20261018`.
- Six additive recipe/resource/catalogue files, preserving existing runtime source and recipe engine in this repository.

## Selected algorithm and behaviour
A bounded entry-less primitive `int[]` open-addressed row+1 hash directory prepares mapped UTF-16 spellings, with exact Unicode/Java String comparison on candidates. Loaded <=50%, refuses >64 collision probes, tiny/large images and pressure. The unchanged sorted binary lookup remains complete semantic fallback; direct rank -> fixed mapped pointer stays O(1). No image schema, String API, fixed OS pointer, JNI ABI or interning representation change.

## Evidence, limitations and gates
Standalone Java 21 oracle **105,494 differential checks** across 5,494 UTF-16 spellings including Java hash collisions and unpaired surrogates: PASS; diagnostic same-host warm loop 166.18 ns vs 313.62 ns (hash vs binary). NOT M3JDK21 product speed evidence.

OpenRewrite Maven/fixed-point replay, actual M3JDK21 JNI contract proof, product modified String/HotSpot jtreg, memory-pressure and cross-platform benchmarks **remain to be run**; keep draft. Catalogue records donor categories including LeetCode, HackerRank and GeeksforGeeks as reference-only; no external source is copied.

canonical.head: 87219f9b837e78cb317e9ebee91334269a5f1668
canonical.body:
## Why this atom

Use Apple Swift Collections' experimental RopeModule/BigString as an **algorithmic donor**, not as a runtime dependency or source-copy donor. The recipe creates a first-party Java 21 M3 BigString implementation in the legacy M3 core text source root.

## Delivered

- `M3Jdk21BigStringRopeSummaryRecipe` composes the existing `M3HashPinnedJavaSnapshotRecipe`; no parallel OpenRewrite engine.
- Exact SHA-256 manifest for two ABSENT targets: `M3BigString.java` and `M3BigStringSelfTest.java`.
- Flat chunk refs plus primitive B-tree index/summary lanes (`int[]`, `long[]`, `byte[]`), 32-way fan-out, long UTF-16 coordinates, source range views, exact Java String hash summaries, surrogate/CRLF boundary summaries, literal KMP across chunks and a candidate-only character bloom.
- `Pattern`/Matcher semantics remain JDK-owned. The facade fails closed when a range exceeds JDK int-indexed CharSequence limits.
- Named standalone Maven proof for first application, exact source postimages, fixed point, all partial-resume subsets, stale-template refusal and foreign-type refusal.
- Donor/algorithm and license disposition catalogue; no Swift source copied and no Swift dependency added.

## Qualification status

The standalone Java implementation and deterministic contract test were run locally with strict Java 21 compilation and `-Xlint:all -Werror` and reported 3,213 assertions, including a synthetic 2.2-billion-code-unit rope backed by repeated references to a 1 MiB chunk. This proves the isolated algorithm only.

**Not yet qualified:** canonical Maven/OpenRewrite tests on this branch, complete M3 core/module build, Java/JNI parity, OpenJDK image integration, adversarial benchmark/GC tests, and production String/regex integration. Keep this draft until hosted Maven tests and the receiver's exact-head gates pass. The recipe manifest pins the template bytes; any failure must be fixed in the recipe/templates, not by manually modifying generated receiver output.

## Scope
- Inspected `apple/swift-collections@b905c889ff75059b8ef0bde480fe55948147b1e6`, specifically RopeModule/BigString. Its regex engine is **not** in BigString; the matching-language donor is `swiftlang/swift-experimental-string-processing`.
- Add an original Java 21 `M3RopeTextIndex` source template (no Apple code copied) with 16-way primitive-indexed node arrays, immutable M3StringPiece references, UTF-16 long offsets, bounded no-copy Matcher windows, and cross-segment KMP.
- Add differential test source, SHA-256 absent-before manifest and candidate/provenance README. Existing M3Index/M3String owners and leaf-cursor/regex recipe crates remain authoritative.

## Verification executed outside GitHub
Exact source fixture compiled using Java 21 and verified **83,941 checks** under JIT, interpreter, non-compact String, C2-focused configurations. Randomized UTF-16, malformed surrogate seams, Java Pattern captures, and a logical 2.2B-code-unit shared-piece composition were covered.

## Unqualified / blockers
**DRAFT: do not merge.** Maven/OpenRewrite recipe replay/fixed-point/refusal, full Synexia reactor, GitHub CI, product JDK build, installed-image jtreg/JCK, JNI/HotSpot/GC, performance and memory A/B were **NOT_EXECUTED**. This source-sealed packet is a candidate handoff, not a runtime promotion. Confirm target code acceptance and reconcile against the existing recipe owners before merge.

receivers.head: ee30cc21886fbeb764c2dd46a544ce46a21e325a
receivers.body:
## Receives canonical Synexia recipe

Canonical recipe-first source and test packet: [com.synexia PR #12347](https://github.com/hsoliwal/com.synexia/pull/12347). That PR owns the SHA-256 template manifest, existing OpenRewrite engine integration, recipe tests, donor/license catalogue, and source-scope inference for the M3 core legacy roots. The generated Java source and proof in this PR are byte-for-byte template postimages.

## Implementation

- New `com.m3.text.M3BigString`: immutable, long-indexed UTF-16 string composition using a 32-way B-tree encoded in primitive coordinate/summary lanes (`int[]`, `long[]`, `byte[]`) and a flat reference directory. There are no per-tree-node Java objects or per-character objects.
- Batched `concat` reuses immutable `String`/`M3StringPiece` chunks and their summaries rather than flattening character data. Long-coordinate subsequence views reuse the same immutable backing/index.
- Subtree summaries include UTF-16 length, code-point count, CR/LF-aware line terminator count, exact Java String hash, ASCII and edge flags, plus a 64-bit character bloom used only as a conservative candidate filter.
- KMP literal search crosses chunk boundaries and returns long range-relative coordinates; `appendTo` streams chunks. `flatten` explicitly refuses above the contiguous Java String limit.
- `Pattern` remains the regex semantic authority through a non-flattening CharSequence for int-sized views. Larger text is refused at this JDK boundary; no unsupported long-index regex equivalence is implied.
- Existing `M3StringPiece`, `M3StringTuple` and `M3Index`/mask/rank owners are not replaced. No Swift code copied and no Swift dependency added.

## Local algorithm proof

The isolated deterministic Java 21 proof passed `javac --release 21 -Xlint:all -Werror` and 3,213 checks, including Unicode/surrogate and CRLF boundaries, random chunk/range differential checks, literal search across boundaries, stock Pattern use, and a synthetic 2,200,000,000-code-unit rope backed by repeated references to a single 1 MiB chunk.

## Hold points

Keep draft until the exact Synexia OpenRewrite Maven test and this receiver's hosted checks pass. The full M3 core build, source integration with every existing owner, JDK image/String integration, JNI/native differential tests, heap/GC pressure tests, adversarial edge cases and performance benchmarks have **not** been claimed as passed. Any discrepancy in generated output must be fixed in the canonical recipe/template and replayed, not hand-patched in this receiver.

receivers.head: 68a5c2955a7cd01bb54b1ecbca999368c6da43df
receivers.body:
## This is M3JDK21's existing runtime owner
**No M3-on-JDK layer or duplicate String interner.** This changes `m3/core/src/com/m3/text/M3GvasLiteralImage.java` (part of M3JDK21's existing fixed-address JNI substrate) and its existing real JNI contract fixture in place. New documentation and catalogue ledger are additive.

## Canonical source FIRST
The sealed runtime source and test were authored in **Synexia [PR #12387](https://github.com/hsoliwal/com.synexia/pull/12387)**, using the existing named OpenRewrite `M3HashPinnedJavaSnapshotRecipe`:
`com.synexia.m3.GvasPrimitiveHash20261018`.
Both received product Git blobs match the exact canonical source-template Git blobs:
- `M3GvasLiteralImage.java`: `c27d6603b32d9c7f277ed097b70ee8eac174b08b`
- `M3GvasLiteralImageContractTest.java`: `d4af3a34e45b58fb6849b1d8ec85d31fdda7b287`.

The pinned before-source Git blobs were `32f506b95688b6cdc11fdf6573a6baaa9ee608c8` and `8f290382ff8a8cd1ed03df0a1fbc054202ec56f4`. Every Java body comes from the recipe template; no separate target-local recipe engine or Synexia runtime dependency is added.

## One bounded behavioral atom
- Existing `M3GvasLiteralImage.findRow(String)` uses sorted UTF-16 binary search.
- On opening a fully validated immutable `M3GVAS01` image, the candidate optionally builds a <=50% load `int[]` open-addressed primitive row+1 directory; hash over **exact UTF-16** code units with exact source-byte comparison on candidates.
- Defends against excessive probe chains (64 bound), tiny/huge images and heap pressure via refusal of *optional precompute* and original binary-search fallback.
- No per-word Entry/Node, second String store, new native symbol, JNI ABI alteration, image format change, Java public method change, or OS pointer relaxation. Rank -> native address remains direct mapped-offset arithmetic.

## Verification and hold
The source-touched JNI fixture now checks colliding Java hash spellings, 2048 negative probes, existing Unicode/surrogate validity and all original native strict-address / digest / inode / collision contract proofs.
A *separate*, standalone Java21 same-host differential oracle passed **105,494** hit/miss comparisons over 5,494 code-unit strings; one diagnostic warm run was 166.18 ns/hash probe versus 313.62 ns/binary probe (not a HotSpot or M3JDK21 speed claim).

**Draft / HOLD:** actual Maven/OpenRewrite fixed-point, JNI compiled receiver proof, full matched M3JDK21 String/HotSpot build + jtreg, adversarial memory pressure and broader latency/RSS/GC/throughput baselines remain unverified. Do not merge until those gates pass.

## Scope
See `m3/docs/M3_GVAS_HASH_LOOKUP_20261018.md` and `m3/lexicon/gvas-hash-index-catalogue-20261018.tsv`. Follow-on: generation-qualified stable UnicodeX word/concept IDs in canonical M3StringPool and primitive state-mask/offset collection owners.

receivers.head: 658a0cc0ef0b88e474a68a06da8db97ac2e05cda
receivers.body:
## What this implements
- First-party Java21 `com.m3.text.M3RopeTextIndex`: a frozen optional metadata index over existing canonical `M3StringPiece` owners.
- Bounded 16-way array-indexed rope geometry in int/long lanes (offsets, counts, bit masks, subtree UTF-16 units). No per-node Entry objects or duplicate text payload.
- Exact `long` UTF-16 lookup, KMP literal matching across segments, reusable no-copy bounded `CharSequence` projection compatible with standard Java `Pattern/Matcher`. Java captures and anchors remain **window-relative**.
- 83,941-assertion differential Java21 test, target `m3/run-rope-proof.sh` four-mode runner, and source/contract/limitation/provenance guide.

## Source-first handoff
Source-sealed, byte-identical to **[Synexia draft PR #12344](https://github.com/hsoliwal/com.synexia/pull/12344)**. Git blob SHA parity verified for both Java source and test. Apple Swift Collections donor geometry pinned to `b905c889ff75059b8ef0bde480fe55948147b1e6`; BigString has no bundled regex engine. No donor source lines transplanted.

## Verification executed
Standalone exact-source fixture compiled with Java21 lint and ran **83,941 assertions per mode**, all passing under default JIT, `-Xint`, noncompact Strings and C2-focused compilation. Also independently compiled as a Java21 named module with matching results.

## OPEN / merge blockers
**DRAFT ONLY**: Maven/OpenRewrite recipe replay/fixed point/drift refusal has not run (Maven unavailable). The *full actual target module* compile/CI proof script has not run, nor target JDK build, jtreg/JCK, JNI/HotSpot, GC/CDS, A/B heap/CPU/RSS. This PR does not modify `java.lang.String`, installed JDK, M3StringTuple or regex internals and does not claim a complete mutable rope, streaming full-corpus regex, or runtime acceptance. Integrate only after M3 source/target contract gates and existing String receiving-phase protocol succeed.
